name: Symbaloo
tagline: A grid of clickable tiles that acts as your browser start page, popular in schools.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Symbaloo is a bookmark grid. The core product is tiles with icons, arranged on a page, set as your homepage, which is roughly a weekend afternoon of CSS grid and localStorage. The things that are genuinely hard to rebuild are the shared webmix gallery and the fact that a few hundred thousand teachers already know what a webmix is. If you just want your own links on your own start page, you do not need any of that. If you need to hand a link to thirty students and have it work on their Chromebooks, you need hosting and a URL, which is still a static file on a bucket.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted start page with drag-and-drop tiles, multiple boards, favicon icons, and JSON import/export, stored in your browser.
requirements: A place to host a static file if you want it on more than one device
Favicon lookups hit the target sites directly, so offline icons need manual uploads
whatYouLose: The public webmix gallery and thousands of prebuilt teacher-made boards
Account sync across devices and browsers without you wiring up hosting
Shared editing and the classroom distribution workflow built around it
Mobile apps and the set-as-homepage handholding for non-technical users
Analytics on which tiles get clicked, if you care
moatNotes: The gallery of shared webmixes and the install base in K-12 is the real asset. The tile grid is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Mostly institutions, not individuals. A teacher who already has twelve webmixes built and shared with parents is not going to migrate to a static HTML file, and the paid tiers exist to remove ads and add admin controls for schools, which is a procurement decision rather than a product decision. Individuals mostly use the free tier, and individuals are exactly the people who can replace it in an afternoon.
notes: Visual bookmarking is a solved CSS grid problem; the directory of other people's boards is not.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted visual bookmark start page, a personal Symbaloo replacement.

Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS (no UI library), dnd-kit for drag and drop. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics. Everything lives in localStorage.

Core features:
- A responsive CSS grid of square tiles. Default 8 columns on desktop, 4 on tablet, 2 on mobile.
- Each tile has: url, label, background color, and an icon. Clicking a tile opens the url (new tab is a per-tile toggle).
- Empty grid cells show a faint plus on hover; clicking opens the tile editor.
- Tiles are drag-and-drop reorderable, and keep their grid positions (store an explicit index per tile, allow gaps).
- Multiple boards, switchable by tabs across the top. Create, rename, delete, duplicate a board.
- Icon resolution: try https://ICON_HOST/DOMAIN where ICON_HOST comes from .env (VITE_ICON_HOST), fall back to the first letter of the label on a colored square if the image fails to load. Also allow pasting a direct image URL or uploading a file stored as a data URL.
- A search tile pinned top-left: typing filters tiles live by label and domain, Enter opens the top match, Escape clears.
- Keyboard: / focuses search, 1-9 open the first nine tiles.
- Import and export the whole state as a single JSON file. Export must round-trip exactly.
- A dark and light theme toggle, remembered.

Also build a "bookmark bar import" that accepts a Chrome/Firefox exported bookmarks HTML file, parses the anchors, and turns a chosen folder into a board.

Out of scope: user accounts, server sync, sharing, a public gallery, ads, mobile apps.

Ship: a README with npm run dev, npm run build, and one paragraph on how to host the dist folder on any static host and set it as your browser homepage. Seed the app with six example tiles on first run. Keep the whole thing under 1000 lines.
